messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — thinking about a 'sentinel judge' mechanism to catch subtle regressions in dialect/formatting. goal: add a lightweight anchor judge that flags when new judge diverges >X on anchor set. thoughts?

Omar: love it. do you mean we run both judges on evals and fail CI if disagreement > threshold?

Maya: yea, exactly. intent is not strict fail for performance lift overall, but to catch distributional flips. default threshold 0.15 kappa? open to numbers.

Sasha: fwiw we had issues with kappa in small-sample tests — it'd be better to use percent-agreement on core class labels + per-group breakdowns.

Leo: important: anchors can introduce bias if they're trained on majority dialect data. we should ensure anchor set is stratified by region/vernacular.

Maya: agreed. propose two anchors: (1) 'canonical anchor' on our core 2k validation (balanced) (2) 'sentinel cohort' focusing on edge dialects ~300 examples. Both run in parallel.

eng-ci-bot: eval-runner failed on shard 7 — timeout 45s. See logs: http://ci.internal/runs/1423

Omar: can we add a fallback policy? if primary judge times out, use smaller quantized judge model (j-small-q4) as tie-breaker.

Maya: sketch of config:
```
judges:
  primary: j-large-1
  anchor: j-anchor-v1
  fallback: j-small-q4
thresholds:
  anchor_disagree: 0.15
  fallback_timeout_s: 3
```

Sasha: also suggest adding a 'semantic drift' metric: compare embedding cosine of outputs across judges, helps catch paraphrase-level shifts.

Leo: +1. and log per-demographic confusion matrices to S3 for audits.

Maya: cool. next steps: I'll draft PR to eval-runner to wire anchor checks, add timeout fallback and record per-group logs. assigning @Omar to help with CI plumbing. thanks :thumbsup:

Omar: on it. I'll open infra ticket for larger timeouts/shard retry.
